evidence: From the car park at the end of Mt Richmond Road, the track follows the Te Hoiere/Pelorus River for an hour to Emerald Pool, an ideal fishing, swimming and picnicking spot.
From here it is about an hour to the Hacket roadend and picnic area, through a mixture of plantation and native forests.
Just downstream of this area a suspension bridge crosses the Hacket River from where it's a short walk to the car park.

ways.label: Exit to Nelson City over the Bryant Range

start.name: car park at the end of Mt Richmond Road
start.quote: the car park at the end of Mt Richmond Road

evidence: An alternative exit is to walk over the Bryant Range from Middy Creek Hut to Nelson City.
From Middy Creek Hut cross a swingbridge and then climb for 20 min to a junction where the Pelorus Track branches left.
The route leads from Rocks Hut to a junction at Dun Saddle.
To the left the track leads steeply down to Brook Street in Nelson City.

doubts: The alternative exit to Nelson City (via Middy Creek Hut, Rocks Hut, Dun Saddle and Coppermine Saddle) is recorded as a second way; the text has two endings for it (the track to the left down to Brook Street, or the Dun Mountain Trail along the old railway line ending further along Brook Street) and the first is taken. Its start is assumed to be the same Mt Richmond Road end as the main way, since the text only says it leaves from Middy Creek Hut. Rocks Hut is on this exit, not the main way. The main way's direction is the one the page describes; no overall distance is given. The side trips' ref T7/T2 are the Whispering Falls and Chromite Mine map tracks leading to those features. The Roebuck Creek crossing is given the creek's ref T24.
